_readme: name: [lat, lon, level, display, country]. country is a two-letter code (US for every U.S. place); a headline whose only places are outside the US is dropped. level 3 = city/county, 2 = state/province, 1 = country/region. Matching is case sensitive on whole words. Two-letter state codes only match after a comma, e.g. 'Abilene, TX'. Add places freely. County, Parish and Township keys hold one entry or a list of candidates (one per state, Census county centroids from us-atlas); the fetcher picks the candidate whose state matches other places in the story or the outlet's state, and skips the name when it stays ambiguous. Towns added by scripts/gazetteer_towns.py come from GeoNames (CC BY 4.0, geonames.org); a town name found in several states holds a list of candidates and is used only when the story names the state. Abbreviations (OKC, NoVA, DFW, Philly) copy the entry they stand for. A sixth element names the metro a town, county or core city belongs to (scripts/gazetteer_metros.py); _metro_cores, _word_names, _new_names, _context_names, _source_metros and _defaults are used by the tagger to prefer suburbs and counties over a metro's core city, accept English-word town names only in sentence-case headlines, and resolve ambiguous names to the outlet's metro.
